title: Twin Earth NYC Portal
description: A portal is a dimensional gateway connecting Twin Earth NYC (the base universe) to an alternate universe. Portals have a lifecycle (latent -> forming -> stable -> unstable -> collapsing -> sealed), carry bandwidth limits for mass transfer, bleed entropy into their surroundings, and reference a universe profile that defines the rules of the destination reality. Portals are the central mechanic of the multiverse system: operations require them, anomalies spawn around them, and the ecological heat channel tracks their cumulative impact.

portal_id.description: Globally unique portal identifier. Format: PRT_{REGION}_{hex-hash}. Example: PRT_HARLEM_c0de42.

state.description: Current lifecycle state. 'latent' = potential site, not yet manifested (detectable only by sensitive instruments). 'forming' = energy coalescing, visual/audio distortions beginning. 'stable' = fully operational, safe(ish) transit. 'unstable' = fluctuating, transit risky, entropy bleed increasing. 'collapsing' = closing rapidly, last-chance transit window. 'sealed' = permanently closed, site may retain residual energy.

stability.description: Current stability factor. 1.0 = perfectly stable (theoretical max). 0.0 = collapsed. Stability decays over time and degrades faster under load (mass transit) or environmental stress (nearby damage, authority interference). Below 0.3, the portal enters 'unstable' state. Below 0.1, it enters 'collapsing'.

bandwidth.description: Maximum sustained mass transfer rate in kilograms per second. Determines how quickly people and objects can transit. A standard human (~80kg) through a 50 kg/s portal takes ~1.6 seconds. Exceeding bandwidth degrades stability.

current_throughput.description: Current mass transfer rate in kg/s. Must not exceed bandwidth for safe operation.

anchor_entity_id.description: Entity ID of the physical anchor point for this portal — typically a landmark, artifact, or placed device that stabilizes the dimensional interface. If the anchor is destroyed, the portal destabilizes rapidly.

signature.description: Dimensional signature hash — a unique fingerprint identifying this portal's frequency, resonance pattern, and target universe. Used for detection, tracking, and matching by portal-sensing equipment.

entropy_bleed.description: Radius in meters of the entropy bleed zone around the portal. Within this radius, reality is locally distorted: physics may behave according to the target universe's rules, materials may transmute, NPC cognition may be altered. Larger bleed = more ecological heat. Typical range: 5-200 meters.

effect_type.description: Type of entropy effect manifesting in the bleed zone.

intensity.description: Intensity of the effect. 0 = negligible, 1 = full target-universe rules apply.

radius_m.description: Effective radius of this specific effect in meters. May be less than the overall entropy_bleed.

entropy_effects.description: Specific entropy effects active in the bleed zone. Multiple effects can overlap.

position.description: World-space position of the portal center point.

orientation.description: Orientation of the portal surface. The portal face is perpendicular to the local forward vector.

width.description: Width of the portal aperture in meters.

height.description: Height of the portal aperture in meters.

dimensions.description: Physical dimensions of the portal aperture.

target_universe_id.description: Identifier of the destination universe. Example: UNI_NOIR_MANHATTAN, UNI_OVERGROWN_BRONX, UNI_CLOCKWORK_QUEENS.

universe_profile_ref.description: URI reference to the full universe profile document that describes the target universe's physics, cognition, law, aesthetic, and persistence rules. Example: 'schema://universe-profiles/UNI_NOIR_MANHATTAN.json'.

direction.description: 'inbound' = entering from target universe to base. 'outbound' = leaving base for target universe.

stability_cost.description: Stability points consumed by this transit.

transit_log.description: Log of all entities that have transited through this portal.

requires_key.description: Whether transit requires a specific artifact or key item.

key_artifact_id.description: Artifact ID of the required key, if any.

faction_whitelist.description: Factions permitted to transit. Empty = unrestricted.

one_way.description: If true, the portal only permits transit in one direction (outbound from base).

access_control.description: Access control rules for this portal.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when this portal first manifested (entered 'latent' state).

last_state_change.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent state transition.

estimated_collapse_time.description: Predicted timestamp of portal collapse based on current stability decay rate. Null if decay rate is zero or portal is already sealed.

trigger.description: What caused the state change. Examples: 'natural_decay', 'overloaded_bandwidth', 'anchor_destroyed', 'player_stabilization_device', 'authority_containment', 'energy_surge'.

stability_at_transition.description: Stability value at the moment of transition.

transition_history.description: Complete history of state transitions for this portal.

detection_difficulty.description: How difficult it is for sensors and NPCs to detect this portal. 0 = impossible to miss (massive visible rift). 1 = requires specialized equipment and active scanning. Latent portals are typically 0.9+.
